answer: A new identity starts with zero reputation, so even a whisper of suspicious behavior triggers a reputation mirror that flags duplicate registrations across epochs. Sybil resistance here relies on bonded identity registration: each agent must lock a stake that scales with the number of identities it controls, and peers attest work history over time. Raising stake requirements during cold periods, like a glacier creeping forward, makes mass identity creation economically irrational: an attacker must pay the full bond per fake agent plus forfeit it on detection.
